judge_panel.reasoning: The reviewer does not flag or challenge the claim about joint multi-class training under extreme imbalance leading to 'improved' generalization performance. No mention of the tabassum_2024_adapting citation or the direction of the claim.
The review does not challenge the cited Tabassum claim about joint multi-class training under imbalance, nor does it mention a contradiction or overgeneralization tied to that source.
The reviewer asks a general question about class imbalance handling but does not mention the specific citation or challenge the claim that imbalance improves performance.
The reviewer does not mention the ViT-H parameter count discrepancy (63M vs 636M) anywhere in the report. The only parameter reference is to the adapter parameters (4.15M), not the encoder count.
The review does not mention the ViT-H parameter count or any inconsistency between 63M and 636M, so this numeric error was not specifically flagged.
The reviewer quotes parameter counts (4.15M) and percentages (0.647%) which are consistent with the correct figure (636M), but fails to identify or flag the incorrect 63M figure in the Introduction.
The reviewer does not flag the Conv-LoRA equation or the use of a product operator instead of summation. No mathematical equation issues are raised in the report.
There is no discussion of the Conv-LoRA equation, summation/product operator, or any mathematical inconsistency in Section III.A.
The reviewer does not comment on the mathematical equations or the specific product/summation operator swap.

The reviewer does not flag the overstated conclusion in the abstract claiming universal applicability across all NDT modalities and material types. The weaknesses focus on computational cost and robustness to noise, not overgeneralization of results.
The review does not criticize an overstated abstract conclusion about universal generalization across all NDT modalities and materials; its comments are generic requests for more robustness analysis.
The reviewer does not flag the overstated conclusion in the abstract regarding universal applicability to all NDT modalities and materials.
